verses.text: In those days the Philistines gathered their forces to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, "You must understand that you and your men will go out with me in the army."
David said, "Then you will see for yourself what your servant can do." Achish replied, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."
Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in his own town of Ramah. Saul had driven the mediums and spiritists out of the land.
The Philistines assembled and came and set up camp at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and set up camp at Gilboa.
When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid, and terror filled his heart.
He asked the LORD for guidance, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams, by the Urim, or by prophets.
Saul then said to his servants, "Find me a woman who is a medium, so that I may go and ask her." "There is one in Endor," they said.
So Saul disguised himself, putting on other clothes, and at night he and two men went to the woman. "Consult a spirit for me," he said, "and bring up for me the one I name."
But the woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done. He has cut off the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why have you set a trap for my life to get me killed?"
Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As surely as the LORD lives, you will not be punished for this."
Then the woman asked, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" "Bring up Samuel," he said.
When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed at the top of her voice and said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"
The king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What do you see?" The woman said, "I see a spirit coming up out of the earth."
"What does he look like?" he asked. "An old man wearing a robe is coming up," she said. Then Saul knew it was Samuel, and he bowed down with his face to the ground.

Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" "I am in great distress," Saul said. "The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do."
Samuel said, "Why do you ask me, now that the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?
The LORD has done what he said through me. The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hands and given it to one of your neighbours, to David.
Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out his fierce anger against the Amalekites, the LORD has done this to you today.

The LORD will give both Israel and you into the hands of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the army of Israel into the hands of the Philistines."
Immediately Saul fell full length on the ground, filled with fear because of Samuel's words. His strength was gone, for he had eaten nothing all that day and all that night.
When the woman came to Saul and saw that he was badly shaken, she said, "Look, your servant has obeyed you. I took my life in my hands and did what you told me to do.
Now please listen to your servant and let me give you some food so you can eat and have the strength to go on your way."
He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his men joined the woman in urging him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the couch.
The woman had a fattened calf at the house, which she killed at once. She took some flour, kneaded it and baked bread without yeast.
Then she set it before Saul and his men, and they ate. That same night they got up and left.
